Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. 1회차 실전 모의고사 Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

When people asked her, "Isn't it scary down there?" she would reply, "What's there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see." Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, ⓑbut that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle. At 17, she took her first deep dive, ⓓdescended 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend's father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists

solution: 주절의 주어(she)가 플로리다로 이사한 후 해변 탐험을 시작했으므로, 분사구문의 동작이 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일임을 나타내기 위해 완료분사구문 'Having + 과거분사' 형태를 사용한다. move를 과거분사 moved로 변형하여 'Having moved'로 쓰고, 나머지 at, Florida, age, of를 활용하여 'at the age of twelve'로 마무리한다.

When most people were ⓐfascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, ⓑbut that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle. Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. (A)그녀가 12 살에 플로리다로 이주한 후에, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, "These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is ⓒdive in." With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean's wonders.
At 17, she took her first deep dive, ⓓdescended 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend's father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists

Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health.
choices: Earle은 바다의 중요성에 대한 대중의 관심을 높이기 위해 많은 노력을 기울였다.

미션 블루 설립 이후 보호 해양 구역은 2009년에 비해 2023 년 약 8%로 증가했다.
국제자연보전연맹은 미션 블루의 목표 달성을 위해 재정적 지원을 제공한다.

다음 글의 내용을 한 문장으로 요약하고자 한다. 빈칸 (A),
(B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health. Sylvia Earle’s dedicated initiatives, including a digital platform, contributed to reshaping the public’s (A) _____ of marine ecosystems, which ultimately led to the measurable (B) of marine protected areas worldwide.
choices: perception - expansion
consumption - depletion
perception - contamination
ignorance - regulation
exploitation - expansion
solution: (A) perception(인식) Earle이 글로벌 디지털 플랫폼 시작에 중요한 역할을 하며 해양 생태계에 대한 감사함을 키웠다고 했으므로, 대중의 해양 생태계에 대한 '인식'을 의미하는 perception이 적절하다. consumption(소비)과 exploitation(착취)은 해양 자원을 이용하는 부정적 행위를 나타내고, ignorance(무지)는 인식의 부재를 의미하므로 적절하지 않다. (B) expansion(확장) 보호 해양 구역이 2009년 1% 미만에서 2023년 약 8%로 증가했으며 2030년까지 30%를 목표로 한다고 했으므로, 보호 해양 구역의 '확장'을 의미하는 expansion이 적절하다. depletion(고갈)과 contamination(오염)은 해양 환경의 악화를 의미하고, regulation(규제)은 확장이 아닌 관리를 의미하므로 적절하지 않다.

However, there is hope of preserving endangered marine species. (C) There are more whales and turtles today than when I was young because most nations are protecting them from harm." With over 7,000 hours underwater and more than 100 expeditions, Sylvia Earle has made significant contributions to the field of marine science. Her lifelong journey will undoubtedly continue to inspire future generations to protect and preserve the ocean, the blue heart of the planet.
solution: 주어진 문장의 역접 접속사 'However'는 앞에 해양 생물의 위기 상황이 언급되어야 하고, 뒤에는 보존에 대한 희망적인 내용이 이어져야 함을 나타낸다. (C) 이전에는 산호초 파괴와 상어 감소라는 부정적 실태가 제시되고, (C) 이후에는 "모두 사라진 것은 아니다"라며 고래와 거북이의 개체 수 증가라는 희망의 예시가 나온다. 따라서 부정적 상황에서 희망의 흐름으로 전환되는 (C) 자리에 들어가는 것이 자연스럽다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with (A) the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and (B) . Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing.

윗글의 빈칸 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: overcame her fear of deep-sea exploration
challenged gender stereotypes
established new diving records in the ocean
inspired other scientists to study coral reefs
gained recognition for her marine biology research
solution: 빈칸 앞에서 Earle은 남녀 공동 참여가 거부된 Tektite 프로젝트에 참여하지 못했지만, 이듬해 여성으로만 구성된 Tektite II 프로젝트를 이끌었다고 했다. 빈칸 뒤에서 Tektite II 팀이 지구 표면으로 귀환했을 때 우주비행사들의 역사적인 달 착륙에 버금가는 주목을 받으며 영웅이 되었다고 했으므로, 빈칸에는 수중 탐험의 한계를 넘어서는 동시에 성별 고정관념에 도전했다는 내용이 와야 한다. 따라서 ② 'challenged gender stereotypes'가 흐름상 가장 자연스럽다.

Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. 이듬해, 그녀는 전부 여성으로 구 성된 텍타이트II 프로젝트의 리더로 선정되어 다른 해양학 자 네 명과 함께 해저 15미터에서 2주 동안 생활했다. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes. Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem.
Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing.

Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis.
ⓐCovering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓑhave been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon," absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is
ⓒmainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean. While "black carbon" is a harmful material produced by ⓓburning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming. Nevertheless, the ocean's ability to perform this planet saving function depends on its health. Dr. Duarte and his team propose a practicable action plan to restore ocean health and aid in the planet's decarbonization. Their urgent recommendations include protecting at least 30% of the ocean by 2030, rethinking industrial fishing practices, ⓔto restore damaged ecosystems like mangroves and coral reefs, and reducing pollution entering the sea. By prioritizing ocean health, we can unlock its potential as a remedy to climate change and work towards a more sustainable future.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ⑤ⓔ to restore → restoring include는 목적어로 동명사만 취하는 타동사이며, 앞뒤 병렬 구조를 보면 protecting, rethinking, reducing 등 동명사가 나열되고 있다. 따라서 to부정사 to restore를 동명사 restoring으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓐ 주어 the ocean이 지구의 70%를 덮는 능동 관계이므로 현재분사 Covering이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓑ 주어 marine ecosystems가 발견되는 수동 관계이며 과거부터 현재까지 이어지는 내용이므로 수동태 현재완료 have been found가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓒ 동사 has dissolved를 수식하는 부사 mainly가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⓓ 전치사 by의 목적어로 동명사 burning이 올바르게 쓰였다.

밑줄 친 (A)를 우리말로 해석하시오.
During the dive, Earle planted a flag on the seafloor to symbolize the significance of ocean exploration in comparison to space exploration. She associated the moment with Neil Armstrong's first steps on the moon and noted "These accomplishments had a few parallels. The modern world had two 'final frontiers' yet to explore: deep space and the deep ocean." Her achievement in Hawaii was one small step towards the day when human beings would come to know and respect the vast world of life underwater. Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990.
(A)She aimed to shift NOAA's focus from exploiting the ocean's resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean's conservation.

She aimed to shift NOAA's focus from exploiting the ocean's resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. (A) In 1979, Sylvia Earle accomplished a historic achievement off the coast of Oahu, Hawaii. Using the JIM suit, she dove 381 meters deep and walked on the ocean floor unattached for two hours. It was marked as the world's deepest solo dive at that time.
(B) It earned her the title "Her Deepness." As she descended, Earle was charmed by the glowing creatures that flashed like stars against the darkness. Among them were some species she had studied but never seen before, such as the deep sea squid that emits a glowing liquid to defend itself.
(C) The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing.

At 17, she took her first deep dive, ⓐdescending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend's father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation. Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats ⓑ situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women ⓒliving together underwater," she said. The following year, ⓓhaving chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and ⓔchallenged gender stereotypes.

위 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Sylvia Earle: A Pioneer Breaking Ocean and Gender Boundaries
The Tektite Project: How Male and Female Scientists Coexisted Underwater in 1969
Why Deep-Sea Exploration Holds Less Value Than Space Exploration
The Technological Evolution of Scuba Diving Equipment in Marine Science
How Sylvia Earle Failed to Overcome Gender Discrimination in Science
solution: ① Sylvia Earle이 해양 탐험의 지평을 넓히고 성별에 대한 고정관념에 도전하며 선구자 역할을 했음을 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 가장 적절하다. ② Tektite 프로젝트에서 남녀 과학자가 함께 거주한 것이 아니라 여성으로만 구성된 팀이 참여했으므로 글의 핵심을 담지 못한다. ③ 심해 탐사가 우주 탐사보다 가치가 적다는 비교 내용은 지문에 언급되지 않았다. ④ 스쿠버 다이빙 장비의 기술적 진화에 초점을 맞춘 글이 아니라 인물의 탐험과 도전 정신을 다룬 글이다. ⑤ Sylvia Earle이 성차별을 극복하지 못한 것이 아니라 성공적으로 한계를 뛰어넘었으므로 글의 내용과 정반대이다.

Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity guided her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation. Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats ⓑ situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women ⓒliving together underwater," she said. The following year, ⓓhaving chosen to lead the all female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ④ⓓ having chosen → having been chosen 문맥상 Sylvia Earle이 Tektite II 프로젝트를 이끌도록 '선택받은' 수동의 의미이다. 분사구문에서 주어인 she가 선택을 받은 주체이므로 완료형 능동분사구문 having chosen을 완료형 수동분사구문 having been chosen으로 고쳐야 한다. ① 주어(she)가 깊은 다이빙을 하며 '하강하는' 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사 descending이 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 'underwater habitats'를 수식하며 '위치해 있는' 수동의 의미이므로 과거분사 situated가 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 전치사 'of'의 목적어로 쓰인 동명사 구문이며, 'men and women'은 동명사 living의 의미상 주어이므로 능동 형태인 living이 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 과거동사 'pushed'와 접속사 'and'로 연결된 병렬 구조이므로 과거동사 challenged가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, "Isn't it scary down there?" she would reply, "What's there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see."
(A) On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, "These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in." With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean's wonders.
(B) Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico.

위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 대부분의 사람들이 우주 탐사에 매료되었을 때, 깊은 바다의 매력을 먼저 알아보고 탐험했다.
바다 깊은 곳으로 내려가 마주치는 생명체들을 보는 것에서 즐거움을 느꼈다.
12세의 나이에 플로리다로 이주한 후 멕시코만의 해양 생물 들을 관찰하기 시작했다.
태어난 지 만 1세가 되던 첫 생일에 부모님으로부터 수경을 선물로 받았다.
아버지는 수경이 수중 탐험에 도움이 될 것이라며 그녀의 다 이빙을 격려하셨다.
solution: ④ 'On her first birthday in Florida'는 태어난 지 만 1세가 된 생일이 아닌 플로리다로 이주한 후 맞이한 첫 생일을 의미하므로, 만 1세 생일에 수경을 선물받았다는 내용의 선택지는 지문의 내용과 일치하지 않는다. ① 타인들이 우주 탐사에 매료되었을 때 바다의 매력을 먼저 알아보고 탐험했다는 내용은 지문 초반부와 일치한다. ② 바다 깊은 곳의 생명체들을 보는 것에서 즐거움을 느꼈다는 답변은 지문 초반부와 일치한다. ③ 12세에 플로리다로 이주한 후 멕시코만의 해양 생물들을 관찰하기 시작했다는 내용은 지문 중반부와 일치한다. ⑤ 아버지가 수경 선물과 함께 수중 탐험을 격려했다는 내용은 지문 후반부와 일치한다.

Earle was appointed the first female chief scientist at the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) in 1990. She aimed to shift NOAA's focus from exploiting the ocean's resources to prioritizing ocean research and conservation. Despite her efforts, Earle, as a senior official of the government, faced restrictions on her freedom of speech and action. Therefore, she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself. Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean's conservation.
choices: 1990년에 NOAA 최초의 여성 수석 과학자가 되었다.

강연, 저술, 과학기술 분야 업무를 통해 해양 보전을 옹호해 왔다.
solution: ③ 지문에서는 Earle이 정부 고위 관리로서 언론과 행동의 자유에 제약을 받았다고 했을 뿐, 예산이나 인력 지원을 충분히 받지 못했다는 내용은 언급되지 않았으므로 일치하지 않는다. ① 1990년 NOAA 최초의 여성 수석 과학자로 임명되었다는 내용과 일치한다. ② NOAA의 초점을 해양 자원 개발에서 해양 연구 및 보전으로 전환하려 했다는 내용과 일치한다. ④ 2년 후 사임하고 더욱 적극적인 환경 운동가가 되었다는 내용과 일치한다. ⑤ 강연, 저술, 과학기술 분야 업무를 통해 해양 보전을 위해 활동해 왔다는 내용과 일치한다.

Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
(A) While "black carbon" is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
(B) This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon," absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean.
(C) For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land.
solution: 주어진 글은 바다가 대기 중 이산화탄소를 흡수하는 중요한 역할을 한다는 배경을 소개한다. (C)는 켈프 숲과 습지 등 해양 생태계가 육지 식물보다 탄소를 더 많이 포집하고 저장한다는 내용을 구체화한다. (B)의 지시어 'This captured carbon(이 포집된 탄소)'은 (C)에서 설명한 포집된 탄소를 지칭하며 이를 '블루 카본'으로 정의한다. (A)는 (B)에서 소개된 '블루 카본'과 대비되는 '블랙 카본'의 위험성을 설명하며 글을 마무리한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as . Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon," absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean. While "black carbon" is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.

위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 기후 변화로 인해 바다의 온도와 산성도가 증가하고 있다.
'블랙 카본'은 화석 연료 연소 시 발생하며 지구 온난화를 방 지하는 역할을 한다.
Carlos Duarte 박사에 따르면 바다는 육지보다 16배 더 많 은 탄소를 보유하고 있다.
켈프 숲과 습지 같은 해양 생태계는 육지 식물보다 탄소 포 집 및 저장 능력이 뛰어나다.
'블루 카본'은 대기에서 흡수되어 바다에 저장된 이산화탄소 를 주로 의미한다.
solution: ② '블랙 카본'은 화석 연료 연소 시 발생하여 기후 변화를 유발하는 물질이고 지구 온난화를 방지하는 것은 '블루 카본'이므로, '블랙 카본'이 지구 온난화를 방지한다는 선택지의 내용은 지문의 내용과 정반대이다. ① 기후 변화로 바다의 온도와 산성도가 증가하고 있다는 내용은 지문 첫 문장과 일치한다. ③ 두아르테(Duarte) 박사에 따르면 바다가 육지보다 16배 더 많은 탄소를 보유한다는 내용은 지문 중반부와 일치한다. ④ 켈프 숲과 습지 같은 해양 생태계가 육지 식물보다 탄소 포집 및 저장 능력이 뛰어나다는 내용은 지문 중반부와 일치한다. ⑤ '블루 카본'이 대기에서 흡수되어 바다에 저장된 이산화탄소를 의미한다는 내용은 지문 후반부와 일치한다.

위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ④ⓓ restored → restoring 동사 include의 목적어로 동명사구(protecting..., rethinking..., restoring..., reducing...)들이 접속사 and로 연결된 병렬 구조이다. 따라서 과거분사 restored를 동명사 restoring으로 고쳐야 한다. ① 주어가 단수 명사구인 'the ocean's ability ~'이므로 단수 동사 depends가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② 명사구 'action plan'을 수식하는 형용사 practicable이 올바르게 쓰였다. ③ 주어가 복수 명사구인 'Their urgent recommendations'이므로 복수 동사 include가 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 명사 'pollution'을 뒤에서 수식하며 '유입되는' 능동의 의미이므로 현재분사 entering이 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was (A) [able / unable] to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all- female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender (B)
[stereotypes / equalities]. Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. ㉠ Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. ㉡ Coral reefs are widely known to face threats due to rising global seawater temperatures. ㉢ The all-female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface. ㉣ They received attention
(C) [similar / indifferent] to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing. ㉤ Their academic success effectively disproved the biased notions held by the authorities.

다음 글의 내용을 바탕으로 요약문의 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들 어갈 알맞은 단어를 영문 본문에서 찾아 각각 한 단어로 쓰시오.
Although Sylvia Earle faced discrimination and was excluded from the first Tektite Project, she later successfully led Tektite II, through which she broke gender (A) _____ and contributed to the field of marine biology by publishing her scientific (B) _____ about coral reef fishes.
(A) _____
(B) _____
solution: 그녀는 성별 ( A )을 깨뜨렸다'에는 지문의 첫 번째 단락 마지막 문장 'she pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes.' (그녀는 수중 탐사의 경계를 넓히고 성별 고정관념에 도전했다)를 참고한다. 이는 '성별 고정관념을 깨고 도전했다'는 문맥이 성립하므로 stereotypes가 알맞다. '산호초 물고기에 대한 그녀의 과학적 ( B )을 출판함으로써'라는 의미의 문장에는 지문의 두 번째 단락 첫 문장 'Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes." (산호초 물고기 생물학을 포함한 그녀의 과학적 발견들이 출판되었다) 를 참고한다. 이는 출판된 대상인 과학적 '발견/연구 결과'를 뜻하는 findings가 알맞다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was (A) [able / unable] to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all- female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender (B)
[stereotypes / equalities]. Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. ㉠ Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. ㉡ Coral reefs are widely known to face threats due to rising global seawater temperatures. ㉢ The all-female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface. ㉣ They received attention
(C) [similar / indifferent] to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing. ㉤ Their academic success effectively disproved the biased notions held by the authorities.

윗글에서 밑줄 친 ㉠~㉤ 중 전체 내용과 관계가 없는 문장은?
solution: ㉡의 산호초가 지구 해수면 온도 상승으로 인해 위협에 처해 있다는 내용은 이 단락의 핵심 흐름인 'Tektite II 프로젝트의 과정과 젠더 장벽 극복 성과'라는 서사와는 전혀 관계가 없으므로 정답은 ②㉡이다.

When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, "Isn't it scary down there?" she would reply, "What's there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see." Long before others, this person recognized that
ⓐnot only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.

위 지문의 밑줄 친 ⓐ 문장을 활용하여 다음 조건에 맞게 영작하시오.
조건 1. 'not only A but also B' 구문을 활용할 것.
2. 부정어구 not only가 문장의 맨 앞으로 가면 서 주어와 동사의 어순이 바뀌는 '도치 (Inversion) 구조'를 정확히 반영할 것.
실비아 얼은 용감할 뿐만 아니라, 지혜롭기도 하다. (동사는 현재 시제 is를 활용할 것)
보기 Sylvia Earle / brave / wise / is (필요 시 단어를 중복 사용하거나 변형할 수 있음.)
→Not only _____ .
answer: is Sylvia Earle brave, but she is also wise (또는 but also wise)
solution: 본문의 주어와 동사 구조인 Sylvia Earle is brave에서 부정을 뜻하는 상관접속사 Not only를 문장의 맨 앞으로 빼내면 주어와 be동사의 위치가 뒤바뀌는 의무적 도치 현상이 발생한다. 따라서 Not only is Sylvia Earle brave 구조가 완성되며, 대등 연결을 이루는 뒷부분은 but she is also wise 또는 주어와 be동사를 생략한 but also wise 형태로 기술한다. YBM(박) 4과

choices: She preferred exploring deep space rather than diving into the vast ocean.

solution: ⑤ 남들이 두렵지 않냐고 묻는 깊은 바다를 적극적으로 탐험하고 그 속에서 기쁨을 느꼈다는 진술을 통해, 미지의 세계에 대한 강한 열정과 용기 있는 태도를 지녔음을 합리적으로 추론할 수 있다. ① 대다수의 사람들과 달리 우주가 아닌 바다의 매력을 인정했다고 했으므로 추론이 올바르지 않다. ② 밑바닥에 무엇이 무섭냐고 반문하며 바다 생명체를 보고 즐거워했으므로 공포를 느꼈다는 추론은 올바르지 않다. ③ 바다가 보호받아야 할 필요가 있음을 일찍이 인지했으므로 상업적 개발을 중시했다는 것은 올바르지 않다. ④ 다른 많은 사람들보다 '먼저(before many others)' 바다의 가치를 알아챘으므로 늦게 시작했다는 것은 올바르지 않다.

Earle has unreservedly dedicated her entire existence to elevating public awareness regarding the indispensable value of our oceans. In 2009, her lifelong endeavors received global recognition due to three milestone achievements. (A) _____ , she played a monumental role in launching a comprehensive digital map platform that enables global citizens to navigate subaquatic environments virtually, thereby encouraging a deeper respect for marine life. (B) _____ , she was honored with the prestigious TED Prize, an esteemed distinction that grants its recipients a transformative wish to heal the planet, supplemented by substantial financial backing.

Write a sentence that matches the given Korean meaning, following the conditions below.
조건 1. 'A에 바치다'를 뜻하는 동사구 구문인 commit oneself to A 구조를 반드시 활용할것.
2. 필요 시 단어 형태를 변형할 것.
3. 각 제시어를 한 번씩만 사용할 것.
얼은 해양의 중요성에 대한 대중의 인식을 높이는 데 평생 을 바쳐왔다.
보기 Earle / the / of / to / public awareness / oneself / commit / raise / the / importance / ocean / of / lifetime / a / about
→
answer: Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean.
solution: 주어 Earle 뒤에 '바치다'라는 뜻의 동사 commit을 '~ 해왔다'라는 의미가 되도록 현재완료 시제인 has committed로 바꾸고, 구문 조건에 맞게 oneself를 주어에 맞춘 재귀대명사 herself와 전치사 to로 연결한다. 이어서 전치사 to 뒤에 명사구인 a lifetime of를 붙인 후, 전치사 of 뒤 동사 raise를 동명사 raising으로 변형해 목적어인 public awareness와 결합한다. 마지막으로 이 대중의 인식을 수식하도록 전치사구 about the importance of the ocean을 순서대로 이어 붙여 문장을 완성한다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the diverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, "These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in." With her goggles, Earle gained a clearer view of the ocean's wonders. At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend's father. Earle was thrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in ⓑcapturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓒhave been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon,"
ⓓabsorbing from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that ⓔhas dissolved directly in the ocean. ⓐincreasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in ⓑcapturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes ⓒhave been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon,"
ⓓabsorbing from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that ⓔhas dissolved directly in the ocean. 위 지문의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 옳은 것만을 있는 대 로 모두 짝지은 것은?
solution: ⓐ 앞 문장의 주어인 기후 변화(Climate change)가 주체로서 뒤의 목적어인 온도와 산도(its temperature and acidity)를 능동적으로 상승시키는 인과 관계를 이룬다. 따라서 현재분사 형태의 분사구문 increasing은 옳다. ⓑ 전치사 in 뒤에 동명사 목적어가 위치하는 자리이다. 타동사 성질을 유지한 동명사 capturing이 뒤에 명사 목적어인 이산화탄소(carbon dioxide)를 정상적으로 수반하고 있으므로 구조상 옳다. ⓒ 복수 주어인 해양 생태계(marine ecosystems)가 탄소를 육지 식물보다 더 잘 가둔다는 학술적 연구 결과를 통해 '발견되어 온' 대상(수동)이다. 수 일치와 시제, 그리고 수동태 규칙을 충족하는 have been found 형태는 옳다. ⓔ 선행사인 이산화탄소(carbon dioxide)를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사 that절 내부의 본동사 자리이다. 이산화탄소 자체가 바다에 직접 '녹아 들어간' 주체(능동)이며 선행사가 단수이므로, 3인칭 단수 현재완료형인 has dissolved는 어법상 아주 정확하다. ⓓ 선행사 명사인 포집된 탄소(This captured carbon)를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사구의 구조이다. 탄소의 입장에서는 대기로부터 스스로 흡수하는 능동의 주체가 아니라 흡수 '되는' 수동의 객체이므로, 현재분사(absorbing)를 과거분사인 absorbed로 수정해야 한다.

블랙 카본의 발생량이 증가할수록 해양의 온도는 점차 감소 할 것이다.

육지 식물은 해양의 습지보다 오랜 기간 동안 더 많은 양의 탄소를 성공적으로 저장해 왔다.

solution: ① 해양 생태계(켈프 숲, 습지 등)가 육지 식물보다 탄소를 더 잘 가두어 저장한다고 했으므로, 이 생태계가 파괴되면 대기 중 탄소를 줄이기가 더 어려워질 것임을 합리적으로 추론할 수 있다. ② 블랙 카본은 기후 변화의 주요 원인이므로 발생량이 늘면 해양 온도는 상승한다. ③ 바다가 지구의 70%를 덮고 있어 이산화탄소 포집에 필수적 역할을 하므로, 면적이 줄면 효율은 떨어진다. ④ 해양 생태계가 탄소 저장 면에서 육지 식물을 능가해 왔으므로 추론이 성립하지 않는다. ⑤ 화석 연료 사용 중단이 바다 속 이산화탄소의 즉각적인 대기 전량 방출을 의미하지 않는다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
(A) Sylvia Earle’s journey began in 1935 when she was born in New Jersey. Having relocated to Florida at the age of twelve, she commenced her exploration of local coastlines, closely ⓐwatching the abundant aquatic life inhabiting the Gulf of Mexico. To celebrate her first birthday after their relocation, her parents presented her
ⓑwith a pair of swimming goggles—a gift exceptionally suited for an ocean enthusiast. Her father offered heartfelt encouragement, ⓒnoted, "These tools will assist you greatly in your underwater endeavors. Now, your only task is ⓓto dive right." Equipped with these goggles, Earle ⓔcould be secured a far more distinct perspective of the sea's magnificent marvels.
(B) Fueled by her inherent craving for adventure and intellectual curiosity, her academic path was skillfully guided, eventually transforming her into a foundational figure in the realms of ocean exploration and habitat conservation.
(C) Upon turning 17, she executed her inaugural deep descent, venturing 10 meters down into a lake while outfitted in a heavy diving suit owned by her friend’s father. Earle experienced immense thrill as she monitored fish while inhaling and exhaling quite effortlessly underwater.
(D) As she became increasingly familiar with the sheer exhilaration of diving, her passion for exploration intensified, ultimately positioning her as one of the pioneering marine scientists to adopt the use of self- contained underwater breathing apparatus (scuba) gear.

주어진 글 (A)에 이어질 내용을 순서에 맞게 배열한 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
solution: 주어진 글 (A)에서 12세 이후 부모님께 고글을 선물 받아 바다에 매료된 일화에 이어, (C)에서 "Upon turning 17(17세가 되었을 때)"라는 구체적인 나이와 함께 생애 첫 깊은 잠수 경험이 시간 순서상 자연스럽게 연결된다. 이어 (D) 는 (C)의 마지막 문장에 나온 잠수 시 느낀 짜릿함을 "the sheer exhilaration of diving(잠수의 순전한 짜릿함)"으로 받아치며 스쿠버 장비를 사용하는 과학자로 성장하는 과정을 보여준다. 마지막으로 (B)에서 이러한 모험심과 지적 호기심을 바탕으로 학문적 길을 걸어 결국 해양 탐사 및 보존 분야의 거두(foundational figure)로 최종 성장했다는 결론으로 마무리하는 것이 가장 적절하다.

다음 글 (A)의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 올바른 것만을 고 른 것은?
solution: ⓐ 주절의 주어인 실비아 얼(she)이 관찰하는 주체이므로 부대상황(동시동작)을 나타내는 현재분사구문의 형태 watching은 올바르다. ⓑ '~에게 ...을 선물하다'라는 뜻의 표준 구문 present A with B을 올바르게 사용하였다. ⓓ is 동사의 주격 보어 자리로, '제대로 뛰어드는 것이다'라는 명사적 의미를 완성하는 to부정사 to dive는 올바르다. ⓒ 문맥상 아버지가 격려를 제공하며 '말하면서/ 덧붙이면서'라는 능동의 분사구문이 되어야 하므로, 과거분사 (또는 과거동사) 형태인 noted를 현재분사인 noting으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ 실비아 얼(Earle)이 바다의 경이로운 장관을 '직접 포착하고 볼 수 있었다'는 능동의 의미가 되어야 하므로, 수동태인 could be secured를 능동태인 could secure로 고쳐야 한다. 따라서 어법상 올바른 것만을 고른 것은 ②ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ이다.

다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Earle has committed ⓐherself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

2. 전치사 to 뒤에는 동명사(Gerund) 형태를 정 확히 기입할 것.
실비아 얼은 해양 과학을 발전시키는 데 그녀의 평생을 바쳤다.
보기 advancing / marine science / her lifetime / Sylvia Earle / to (필요 시 단어를 변형하거나 대명사를 재귀형태 로 적절히 조합할 수 있음.)
→ _____ .
answer: Sylvia Earle committed her lifetime to advancing marine science
solution: 주어인 Sylvia Earle 뒤에 동사 committed를 배치하고, 기여하는 대상 목적어인 her lifetime(그녀의 평생)을 위치시킨다. 그 뒤에 전치사 to를 붙이고 전치사의 목적어 역할을 수행할 수 있도록 동명사 형태인 advancing과 그 대상인 marine science를 순차적으로 연결하여 배열한다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Earle has committed ⓐherself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, which allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostering appreciation for marine ecosystems. She was also awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally, this wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aims to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is to protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health.

위 지문의 밑줄 친 ⓐherself와 쓰임이 다른 것만을 <보기 >에서 있는 대로 고른 것은?
보기 (A) Sylvia Earle herself gave an inspiring public lecture to the students.
(B) The marine biologist introduced herself to the international committee.
(C) The deep-sea creatures protect themselves by flashing glowing liquids.
(D) We must clean the contaminated beaches ourselves before the storm hits.
(E) The non-profit organization itself does not require financial profits. (F) She often blamed herself for the government's restrictions on free speech.
solution: 지문의 ⓐherself: 문장에서 목적어 역할을 하며 생략할 수 없는 '재귀 용법'으로 사용된 재귀대명사이다. (A) herself가 주어(Sylvia Earle)를 강조하며, 이를 제외해도 주어와 동사가 있는 완전한 문장이 된다. (강조 용법) (B) 주어(생물학자)가 '자기 자신'을 소개하는 문맥으로, 동사의 목적어이며 생략이 불가능하다. (재귀 용법) (C) 주어(심해 생물들)가 '자신들'을 보호하는 문맥으로, 동사의 목적어이며 생략이 불가능하다. (재귀 용법) (D) ourselves가 주어 We를 강조하며, 이를 지워도 주어· 동사·목적어가 모두 있는 완전한 문장이 된다. (강조 용법) (E) itself가 주어 organization을 강조하며, 이를 지워도 완전한 문장이 된다. (강조 용법) (F) 주어(She)가 '자신'을 비난하는 문맥으로, 동사의 목적어이며 생략이 불가능하다. (재귀 용법) 따라서 지문의 ⓐherself(재귀 용법)와 쓰임이 다른 것은 강조 용법으로 쓰인 (A), (D), (E)이므로 정답은 ①이다.

(A) , she resigned two years later to become a more active environmental activist. ⓒ Through her work in science and technology businesses, public lectures, and writing books and articles for the mass media, Earle has been able to use her expertise and experience to campaign for the ocean's conservation. ⓓ Earle has committed herself to a lifetime of raising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. ⓔ In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through key events. Returning to the private sector granted Earle the freedom to express herself.

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
At a time when the general public was captivated by the enigmas of outer space travel, a single extraordinary person recognized the magnificent allure of the sea far ahead of her contemporaries, eagerly plunging into the deep waters. Whenever people questioned her, asking, "Are you not terrified down there?" she would invariably respond, "There is absolutely nothing to dread. When I
ⓐdescend into the depths, I find pure joy in the marine life I observe." Far ahead of her time, this individual came to realize that the ocean is not only ⓑteeming with diverse organisms, but it also desperately demands our protection. The individual in question is none other than the legendary marine scholar, Sylvia Earle.

위 지문의 첫 문장의 구조를 참고하여, 주어진 단어를 한글 해석에 맞게 올바른 형태로 변형하여 영작하시오.
대부분의 사람들이 우주에 매료되었던 반면에, 실비아 얼은 깊은 바다를 열정적으로 탐험했다.
보기 by space / While / eagerly / most people / explore / be / fascinate / Sylvia Earle / the deep ocean
→ _____ , _____ .
answer: While most people were fascinated by space, Sylvia Earle eagerly explored the deep ocean.
solution: 지문 첫 문장의 'At a time when ~(~했던 시기에)'처럼 두 상황을 대조하기 위해 문두에 부사절 접속사 While(~한 반면에)을 배치한다. '우주에 매료되었다'는 수동의 의미이므로, 과거 시제에 맞춰 were fascinated by 형태로 쓴다. 이때 주어가 most people 복수이므로 were을 사용한다. 과거의 사실을 서술하고 있으므로, 제시된 동사 explore를 과거형인 explored로 변형하고, 동사를 수식하는 부사 eagerly를 그 앞에 위치시킨다.

Sylvia Earle’s journey began in 1935 when she was born in New Jersey. ㉠ Having relocated to Florida at the age of twelve, she commenced her exploration of local coastlines, closely watching the ⓐabundant aquatic life inhabiting the Gulf of Mexico. To celebrate her first birthday after their relocation, her parents presented her with a pair of swimming goggles—a gift exceptionally suited for an ocean enthusiast. ㉡ Her father offered heartfelt encouragement, noting, "These tools will assist you greatly in your underwater endeavors. Now, your only task is to dive right in." Equipped with these goggles, Earle was able to secure a far more distinct perspective of the sea's magnificent marvels. ㉢ Upon turning 17, she executed her inaugural deep descent, venturing 10 meters down into a lake while outfitted in a heavy diving suit owned by her friend’s father. ㉣ As she became increasingly familiar with the sheer exhilaration of diving, her passion for exploration
ⓑdiminished, ultimately positioning her as one of the pioneering marine scientists to ⓒreject the use of self- contained underwater breathing apparatus (scuba) gear. ㉤ Fueled by her inherent craving for adventure and intellectual curiosity, her academic path was skillfully guided, eventually ⓓ transforming her into a
ⓔfoundational figure in the realms of ocean exploration and habitat conservation.

다음 글의 주제로 가장 알맞은 것을 고르시오.
choices: The technological evolution of heavy diving suits and scuba gear
Sylvia Earle’s early diving experiences and growth into a marine explorer
Environmental threats facing the aquatic life in the Gulf of Mexico
The rigorous academic curriculum required for prospective marine scientists
The socioeconomic challenges of deep-lake exploration in the mid-1900s
solution: 본문은 실비아 얼이 유년 시절 물안경을 통해 바다를 접하고, 17세에 첫 하강을 경험하며 선구적인 해양 과학자 및 보존 생물학자로 성장해 나가는 초기 일화와 과정을 다루고 있다. 따라서 얼의 초기 다이빙 경험과 해양 탐험가로의 성장을 언급한 ②번이 주제로 가장 올바르다. ① 잠수복과 스쿠버 장비의 기술적 진화: 장비는 얼의 성장을 보여주는 수단일 뿐 장비 자체의 역사를 다룬 글이 아니므로 올바르지 않다. ③ 멕시코만 해양 생물이 직면한 환경적 위협: 구체적인 위협 요인은 본문에 언급되지 않으므로 올바르지 않다. ④ 미래 해양 과학자들에게 요구되는 엄격한 학업 교육과정: 얼의 개인적 학문 경로가 유도되었다는 내용만 일부 나올 뿐 일반적인 교육과정을 설명하지 않으므로 올바르지 않다. ⑤ 1900년대 중반 깊은 호수 탐험의 사회경제적 어려움: 탐험의 사회경제적 장벽이나 비용 등은 글의 내용과 전혀 무관하므로 올바르지 않다.

When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, "Isn't it scary down there?" she would reply, "What's there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see." Long before others, this person recognized that 바다가 생명체로 가득 차 있을 뿐만 아니라, 보호받을 필요도 있다는 것을. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle.
보기 full / that / protected / the ocean / is / to be / not only / of life / needs / but / it / also
answer: not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be protected
solution: not only A but (also) B' 구조를 사용하여 'A뿐만 아니라 B도'라는 의미를 나타낸다. recognize의 목적어 역할을 하는 that절 2개가 not only와 but 뒤에 각각 배치된다. 첫 번째 that은 본문에 이미 적혀 있고, 두 번째 that은 but 바로 뒤에 위치하여 that [A], but that [B]의 완벽한 병렬 구조를 이룬다. 첫 번째 절에서는 부정어구(not only)가 맨 앞으로 오면서 주어와 동사가 도치된다. 따라서 평서문 순서가 아닌, 동사가 주어 앞으로 나간 is the ocean full of life가 온다. 두 번째 that 뒤에는 도치 없이 정상적인 주어(it)와 동사(needs) 순서가 온다. 이때 바다는 보호를 '받는' 수동의 대상이므로 needs 뒤에 to be protected가 위치한다.

Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. The following year, having been chosen to lead the all- female Tektite II Project, she spent two weeks living 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes. Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem. Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all-female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface,
ⓐ _____ .

Many families still keep the tradition of celebrating the harvest.
The city is Seoul, the capital of Korea.
solution: ② '그녀의 노트' 또는 '그녀의 휴대폰'처럼 or로 연결된 서로 다른 대상을 나열한 것으로 동격 관계가 아니다. 나머지는 모두 동격 관계이므로 정답은 ②이다. ① a firm belief와 that절의 내용이 같은 것을 가리키는 동격 관계이다. ③ the news와 that the companies would merge는 that절이 news의 구체적인 내용을 설명하는 동격 관계이다. ④ the tradition과 of 이하가 같은 관습을 가리키는 동격 관계이다. ⑤ Seoul과 the capital of Korea가 같은 대상을 가리키는 동격 관계이다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 괄호 안의 말을 이용하여 문장을 완성하시오.
하루 종일 아무것도 사지 않아서, 그는 돈이 많이 남아 있었다.
(buy)
→ _____ all day, he had a lot of money left.
solution: ‘아무것도 사지 않은 것’이 주절보다 앞선 일이므로 완료형 분사구문 Having bought nothing을 써야 한다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장을 고르시오.
choices: Written by a famous author, the novel became an instant bestseller.
Cutting into small pieces, the vegetables will cook faster.
Considering his age, he performs remarkably well in sports.
Being unfamiliar with the software, the new employee asked for help.
The issues discussed earlier will be addressed in the next meeting.
solution: ②는 채소가 작은 조각으로 잘려진다는 수동의 의미이므로 Cutting이 아니라 Cut을 써야 한다. ①은 수동의 과거분사 (Written)로 올바르다. ③은 관용적 표현(considering)으로 올바르다. ④는 Being+형용사의 분사구문으로 올바르다. ⑤는 명사를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사(discussed)로 올바르다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 괄호 안의 말을 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
조건 어느 봄날 저녁의 아름다운 노을에 감동하여, 그녀 는 시인이 되기로 결심했다.
(with, impressed, the beautiful sunset)
→ on a spring evening, she decided to become a poet.
solution: she가 아름다운 노을에 감동한 상태이므로 Impressed with를 쓴다.

body:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
그녀는 캐나다에서 자랐기 때문에 영어를 유창하게 할 줄 안다.
→ _____ in Canada, she can speak English fluently.
choices: Having grown up _____
Grow up
Growing up _____
To grow up
Being grown up
solution: 분사구문이 나타내는 시점이 주절보다 이전이므로 완료형 분사구문 Having grown up을 써야 한다. ②Grow up은 동사 원형으로 분사구문 자리에 올 수 없다. ③Growing up은 ‘캐나다에서 자라는 동안’이라는 진행 의미가 강해, 이미 캐나다에서 성장한 경험이 현재의 영어 능력의 배경이 됨을 나타내는 우리말에는 작절하지 않다. ④To grow up은 to부정사이다. ⑤Being grown up은 수동형인데 she가 자란 행위의 주체이므로 능동형이 되어야 한다.

body:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것을 모두 고르면?
어렸을 때 수줍음이 많았기 때문에, 그녀는 사람들 앞에서 말 을 잘 하고 싶어 한다.
① Was shy as a child, she wants to speak well in front of people.
② Been shy as a child, she wants to speak well in front of people.
③ Shy as a child, she wants to speak well in front of people.
④ Having been shy as a child, she wants to speak well in front of people.
⑤ Being shy as a child, she wants to speak well in front of people.
solution: 형용사(shy) 앞의 Being은 생략이 가능하므로 ③처럼 형용사만 남긴 형태가 옳다. 또한 주절(현재, wants)보다 분사구문이 나타내는 상태(어렸을 때 수줍었음)가 앞서 일어난 일이므로 완료분사 Having been을 쓴 ④도 옳다. ①은 정형동사 Was가 분사 자리에 쓰여 분사구문 형태가 아니므로 틀리다. ②는 having 없이 과거분사 Been만 쓰여 올바른 분사구문이 아니므로 틀리다. ⑤는 단순분사 Being을 써서 시간의 선후 관계가 드러나지 않으므로 틀리다.

body: 다음 밑줄 친 두 부분의 관계가 나머지와 다른 것은?
choices: Mia usually talks to her sister or her cousin about school life.
Jack has a deep concern that he might fail the exam.
The mountain is called K2, the second-highest peak in the world.
Many people today accept the fact that the climate is changing.
Our town still holds the custom of lighting lanterns each spring.
solution: ① '그녀의 언니' 또는 '그녀의 사촌'처럼 or로 연결된 서로 다른 대상을 나열한 것으로 동격 관계가 아니다. 나머지는 모두 동격 관계이므로 정답은 ①이다. ② a deep concern과 that절의 내용이 같은 것을 가리키는 동격 관계이다. ③ K2와 the second-highest peak in the world가 같은 대상을 가리키는 동격 관계이다. ④ the fact와 that the climate is changing은 ‘기후가 변하고 있다는 사실’로, that절이 fact의 구체적인 내용을 설명하는 동격 관계이다. ⑤ the custom과 of 이하가 같은 풍습을 가리키는 동격 관계이다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
There is no reason to feel anxious about circumstances we cannot control, and it drains your motivation to focus on mistakes (A)[that / what] you will probably forget within a few weeks. Handle each setback, minor or major, calmly and try to fix what is happening right now. Learn to stay polite with an impatient customer. Smile at the driver who honks behind you. So it helps to build the habit of finding something positive in every circumstance. (B)[Catching / Caught] in a sudden rainstorm, use the moment to enjoy the fresh air. When you fail an important exam, think of how much you learned while preparing for it. All this does not mean that you should give up trying to prevent future problems. The point is that although fortunate and unfortunate events occur in life, we should practice focusing on the pleasures of daily life, and (C)[learning / to learn] from difficult moments.
choices: that - Caught - learning
that - Catching - to learn
what - Caught - to learn
what - Catching - learning
that - Catching - learning
solution: (A)는 선행사 mistakes가 있으므로 이를 수식하는 목적격 관계대명사 that이 적절하다. what은 선행사를 포함하는 관계대명사이므로 앞에 선행사가 있을 때 사용할 수 없다. (B)는 주어가 갑작스러운 폭우에 ‘갇힌’ 상태이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 Caught가 적절하다. (C)는 전치사 on의 목적어로 쓰인 focusing과 and로 병렬을 이루므로 동명사 learning이 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ①이다.

body: 다음 중 밑줄 친 부분이 어법상 틀린 것은?
choices: It was thrilling to watch students discover their talents through our program.
Having been finished, the students quietly packed their bags and left the classroom.
The workers are repairing roads damaged by the flood.
Being so short, Sarah is often mistaken for a middle school student.
While walking through the park, I was attracted by a sparkling fountain in the distance.
solution: 학생들이 (누군가에 의해) 강제로 끝내진 것이 아니라 능동적으로 한 행동이므로, 수동태 형태인 been을 빼고, 능동형 완료분사구문인 having finished로 써야 올바르다.

body:
밑줄 친 부분을 분사구문으로 바꿔 쓰시오. (접속사는 넣지 말 것)
After they had watched the movie, they discussed the plot together.
→ _____ , they discussed the plot together.
solution: 과거완료시제를 가진 시간부사절을 분사구문으로 바꿀 때, 주절보다 먼저 일어난 동작이므로 완료형 분사구문 'Having + 과거분사'를 사용한다.

body:
(A), (B), (C)의 각 괄호 안에서 어법에 맞는 표현으로 가장 적절한 것은?
James Cook Jr., the first American cartographer recognized by the government, had an eventful early career. At the age of 22, he was wrongly accused of espionage and, to avoid execution, he spent the next 6 years of his life in exile. (A)
[Watching / Watched by] foreign agents, he was forced to travel through remote territories in secret. Although Cook found this dangerous, it gave him valuable knowledge of the terrain, (B)
[enabling / enabled] him to create highly accurate maps of unexplored regions. When he was finally recognized by the government, he had the chance to use his expertise. In exchange for his help in charting a new trade route, Cook (C)
[awarded / was awarded] the recognition he needed to restore his reputation.
choices: Watching - enabled - was awarded
Watched by - enabled - awarded
Watching - enabling - awarded
Watched by - enabling - was awarded
Watched by - enabled - was awarded
solution: (A)는 주어 he가 외국 요원들에게 ‘감시당하는’ 수동의 관계이므로 과거분사 Watched by가 적절하다. (B)는 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문으로, 그 경험이 그로 하여금 정확한 지도를 만들 수 있게 ‘해 주었다’는 능동의 의미이므로 enabling이 적절하다. (C)는 Cook이 인정을 ‘수여받은’ 것이므로 수동태 was awarded가 적절하다. 따라서 정답은 ④ Watched by - enabling - was awarded이다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Students generally become more focused when approaching exams.
Having been told the news, she quickly shared it with her friends.
We will go hiking tomorrow, weather permitting.
Having informed of the decision, he accepted it gracefully.
Judging from the evidence, the conclusion seems reasonable.
solution: 주절의 주어 he와 분사구 Having informed of the decision의 관계는 수동의 관계이다(그가 그 결정에 대해서 알게 된 것). 따라서 완료 분사구문 Having informed를 수동형 Having been informed로 고쳐야 한다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 맞는 것을 고르시오.
choices: Being no salt in the kitchen, she went to the grocery store.
He is waiting for the bus with his legs crossing.
I cut my finger chopping onions for soup.
Being awarding for his bravery, the soldier felt very proud.
If not properly training, the dog might bark at strangers.
solution: ③: O ①: Being → There being 'There is/are' 구문의 분사구문 ②: crossing → crossed 다리는 꼬아지는 대상이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 사용 ④: Being awarding → (Being) Awarded 상을 받은 것이므로 수동의 분사구문 사용 ⑤: training → trained 개가 훈련받는 것이므로 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 사용

body: 다음 중 어법상 어색한 문장을 고르시오.
choices: Being written carefully, the report impressed everyone.
Being seemed confident, she delivered the presentation well.
Before starting the project, we need to prepare the materials.
After finishing homework, the students went out to play.
Being the youngest player on the team, she worked harder than anyone.
solution: ② Being seemed → Seeming : seem은 '~처럼 보이다'라는 뜻의 대표적인 자동사이다. 자동사는 수동태가 불가능하므로 Being seemed라는 표현은 성립할 수 없다. 따라서 현재분사 형태인 Seeming으로 바꿔야 한다.

body:
다음 주어진 우리말과 일치하도록 괄호 안의 어구를 사용하 여 영작하시오. (어형 변화 가능)
그 영화를 여러 번 봤기 때문에, Tom은 모든 대사를 기억하 고 있다. (times, the movie, have, several, watch)
→ _____ ​, Tom remembers every line.
answer: Having watched the movie several times
solution: 완료형 분사구문 'Having + 과거분사'는 주절의 동작보다 먼저 일어난 동작을 나타낸다. 'having watched the movie several times'가 정답이다.

body:
어법상 틀린 부분을 찾아 바르게 고치시오.
Jake constantly ridicules me in our team meetings. As I couldn't bear his inappropriate conduct anymore, I made up my mind to approach the supervisor. Reported the matter to her, I wondered what steps she would take.
→
solution: 주절과 주어가 같으며 주어(I)가 동작을 하는 능동형태이므로 과거분사 reported는 옳지 않다. 또한 부사절이 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 완료분사구문을 사용하여 'Having reported' 형태로 나타내야 한다.

body:
두 문장이 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
After they had watched the movie, the children discussed it together. = _____ the movie, the children discussed it together.
choices: Watching _____
Being watched
Having watched _____
They watching
Having been watched
solution: 부사절의 시제(had watched)가 주절의 시제(discussed) 보다 앞서므로 분사구문으로 바꿀 때 동사를 'having p.p' 형태로 쓴다.

body:
두 문장이 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
Since she is praised by her teacher, she feels happy. = _____ by her teacher, she feels happy.
choices: Since praising _____
Praising
Never praised _____
Praised
Having been praised
solution: 부사절의 동사가 주절과 시제가 같고 수동태이므로 'being p.p' 형태로 쓰는데, 'being'은 생략할 수 있다.

body:
우리말과 같은 의미가 되도록 괄호 안의 말을 이용하여 빈칸 을 완성하시오. (분사구문으로 쓸 것)
햇빛에 노출되면, 그 식물들은 빠르게 자랄 수도 있다.
(expose to, sunlight)
→ _____ , the plants may grow quickly.
solution: ‘햇빛에 노출되면’은 수동의 의미를 나타내므로 과거분사 exposed를 사용하여 Exposed to sunlight가 적절하다.

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐLook at the withered flowers in the vase.
ⓑNo one having raised any objections, the committee approved the plan.
ⓒRecommended by several critics, the small restaurant became very popular.
ⓓAt first I thought the puzzle was a very confusing and frustrating game.
ⓔSupposed there was a power outage, what would you do?
ⓕLearned Spanish in college, he can still write simple sentences.
solution: 정답은 ① e, f이다. e의 'Supposed'는 '만약 ~라면'이라는 뜻의 조건 표현으로 쓰일 때는 원형 'Suppose(Supposing)'를 사용해야 하므로 어법상 틀렸다. → Suppose there was a power outage, what would you do? f는 주어 'he'가 학습이라는 동작을 완료한 주체이므로 완료형 분사구문 'Having learned'를 사용해야 한다. → Having learned Spanish in college, he can still write simple sentences. a는 자동사 'wither'의 과거분사 'withered'가 완료·능동의 의미로 명사를 수식하는 올바른 표현이다. b는 분사구문의 주어(no one)가 주절의 주어(the committee)와 달라 독립분사구문을 사용한 것으로, 완료의 의미를 나타내는 'having raised'가 올바르게 쓰였다. c는 식당이 비평가들에 의해 추천되는 대상(수동)이므로 과거분사 'Recommended'가 올바르게 쓰였다. d는 퍼즐이 다른 사람에게 혼란과 답답함을 유발하는 주체이므로 현재분사 'confusing and frustrating'이 올바르게 쓰였다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: I am sorry to have kept you waiting so long.
They were proud of winning the competition.
Call me when you finish your homework.
When asking the question, she said nothing.
I forgot to turn off the stove before leaving.
solution: ④ asking → asked 분사구문에서 she가 질문을 하는 주체가 아니라 받은 대상이므로 능동형 asking이 아니라 수동 의미의 과거분사 asked를 써야 한다.

body:
다음 문장의 빈칸에 들어갈 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
by a loud noise, the baby began to cry.
choices: Startling _____
To startle
Startled _____
To be startled
Startle
solution: 아기가 놀란 것이므로 수동의 의미를 나타내는 분사구문이 와야 하며, 이는 Being startled의 생략형인 과거분사 Startled로 표현한다.

body:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 괄호 안의 표현을 바르게 배열하시오.
너무 많이 먹은 후에, 그녀는 속이 안 좋았다.
(too much, eaten, having)
→ _____ , she felt sick.
solution: 주절의 동작보다 앞서 일어난 일을 나타낼 때는 'Having + 과거분사' 형태의 완료형 분사구문을 쓴다. 따라서 'Having eaten too much'가 정답이다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장을 고르시오.
choices: Seen from the mountain top, the village looks tiny.
Considering the circumstances, I think we made the right choice.
The students involved will present their projects next week.
Using carefully, this tool will last for many years.
Being too tired to continue, he decided to stop working for the day.
solution: ④는 도구가 조심스럽게 사용된다는 수동의 의미이므로 Using이 아니라 Used를 써야 한다. ①은 수동의 과거분사 (Seen)로 올바르다. ②는 관용적 분사구문(Considering) 으로 올바르다. ③은 명사를 뒤에서 수식하는 분사(involved) 로 올바르다. ⑤는 Being+형용사의 분사구문으로 올바르다.

body:
다음 밑줄 친 (A), (B)의 올바른 형태로 알맞게 짝지어진 것은?
When (A)ask what she was planning for this summer, Sarah said, "I'm excited about (B)visit Europe and exploring new cultures."
choices: asking - visiting _____
asks - visit
asked - visiting _____
asked - visit
asking - visited
solution: (A) asked: 사라가 무엇을 계획하는지 질문 받았을 때(수동) 의 맥락입니다. 주어인 사라가 이야기를 질문을 받은 입장이므로 과거분사 told가 적절하다. (B) visiting: 전치사(about) 뒤에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로, 동명사 visiting이 정답이다.

body:

the report, she submitted it to her manager.
choices: Complete _____
Having completed

solution: 보고서를 완성한 것이 제출한 것보다 먼저 일어난 일이므로 완료분사구문 Having completed가 적절하다.

body: 다음 중 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.
choices: Do you know the girl standing near the gate?
For entertainment, I prefer watching movies to playing games.
Adjusting properly, this equipment will operate smoothly for years.
He had to stop cycling because of back problems.
We were talking about whether the offer was worth accepting.
solution: ③ 'Adjusting properly, this equipment will operate smoothly for years.'에서 분사구문의 주어인 equipment는 스스로 조정하는 것이 아니라 조정되는 대상이므로 능동분사 Adjusting이 아니라 과거분사 Adjusted를 써야 한다. → Adjusted properly, this equipment will operate smoothly for years. ① 현재분사구가 명사 the girl을 뒤에서 수식하는 구조로 올바르게 쓰였다. ② prefer A to B 구문에 동명사가 쓰여 올바르다. ④ stop + 동명사 구조로 올바르다. ⑤ worth + 동명사 구조로 올바르다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는?
Improved consumer awareness about food waste may be the cheapest way to save the most food, but it ⓐis not the only way for consumers to contribute to food waste reduction. ⓑWith composting technology spreading faster than ever before, there are plenty of devices ⓒleading to reduction food waste by helping us to compost more efficiently. More than 20 models of smart composters are on the market today, ⓓsome of them processing more than five pounds of food waste per day. ⓔThough expensive a few years ago, these composters are affordable now and can help the average household reduce food waste significantly. Appliances officially certified as most efficient are tagged with the Eco Star logo to alert the shopper. Smart composters with that rating process food scraps twice as fast as older models. High-efficiency dehydrators save even more food. These devices ⓕhelp us not to waste as much food as we did with older models.
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution: 정답은 ①(1개)이다. ⓒ의 'reduction food waste'는 복합명사 어순이 잘못되어 'food waste reduction'이 되어야 한다. 나머지 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓓ, ⓔ, ⓕ는 모두 어법상 올바르며, 각각 'for+목적어+to부정사', 'with+명사+현재분사'의 능동 분사구문, 'some of them+현재분사' 구문, 'Though+형용사'의 분사구 축약, 'help+목적어+(to) 동사원형' 구조를 올바르게 사용하였다.

body:
주어진 문장과 같은 뜻이 되도록, 빈칸에 알맞은 분사 구문 을 쓰시오.
She had studied French in Paris, so she spoke it fluently. = _____ she spoke it fluently.
solution: 주절보다 시간적으로 앞선 상황을 나타내므로 완료 분사구문 'Having + p.p.'를 사용한다. 따라서 'Having studied French in Paris,'가 정답이다.

body:
다음 중 어법상 틀린 문장끼리 짝지어진 것은?
ⓐSupposed the flight was canceled, what would you do next?
ⓑStudied Chinese for years, he can still hold a basic conversation.
ⓒLook at the frozen lake behind the cabin.
ⓓNo one having volunteered for the project, the director felt anxious.
ⓔAt first I thought the documentary was a very confusing and depressing film.
ⓕFeatured in several international magazines, the young designer gained much attention.
solution: 정답은 ⑤ a, b이다. a의 'Supposed'는 '만약 ~라면'이라는 뜻의 조건 표현으로 쓰일 때는 원형 'Suppose(Supposing)'를 사용해야 하므로 어법상 틀렸다. → Suppose the flight was canceled, what would you do next? b는 주어 'he'가 학습이라는 동작을 완료한 주체이므로 완료형 분사구문 'Having studied'를 사용해야 한다. → Having studied Chinese for years, he can still hold a basic conversation. c는 자동사 'freeze'의 과거분사 'frozen'이 완료·능동의 의미로 명사를 수식하는 올바른 표현이다. d는 분사구문의 주어(no one)가 주절의 주어(the director) 와 달라 독립분사구문을 사용한 것으로, 완료의 의미를 나타내는 'having volunteered'가 올바르게 쓰였다. e는 다큐멘터리가 다른 사람에게 혼란과 우울함을 유발하는 주체이므로 현재분사 'confusing and depressing'이 올바르게 쓰였다. f는 디자이너가 잡지에 소개되는 대상(수동)이므로 과거분사 'Featured'가 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
두 문장이 같은 의미가 되도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 고르시오.
After he had completed the project, Mike went out for dinner. = _____ the project, Mike went out for dinner.
choices: Having completed
Being completed
Completing
He completing
Having been completed
solution: 부사절의 시제(had completed)가 주절의 시제(went)보다 앞서므로 분사구문으로 바꿀 때 동사를 'having p.p' 형태로 쓴다. YBM(박) 4과 문법 정복 실전

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
Earle ⓐhas committed herself to a lifetime of rising public awareness about the importance of the ocean. In 2009, her efforts gained prominence through three key events. She played an important role in initiating a global digital platform, ⓑwhich allows users to explore underwater worlds virtually, fostered appreciation for marine ecosystems. She ⓒalso awarded the TED Prize, a distinguished annual award that grants winners a wish to change the world, along with financial support. Earle's wish was to create a global network of marine protected areas, or "Hope Spots," which serve as refuges from pollution, overfishing, and other threats. Finally,
ⓓthis wish led her to establish Mission Blue, a non-profit organization that aim to inspire action to explore and protect the ocean. Since its establishment, protected ocean areas have increased from less than 1% in 2009 to approximately 8% in 2023. Mission Blue's goal is
ⓔto protect 30% of the ocean by 2030, in line with the International Union for Conservation of Nature's recommended target for maintaining ocean health.
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution: ⓐ rising → raising '대중의 인식을 높이다'는 의미의 타동사 raise가 필요하므로 자동사 rising을 raising으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓑ fostered → fostering 앞 절의 내용을 부연 설명하는 분사구문으로, 플랫폼이 해양 생태계에 대한 감사함을 키우는 능동의 의미이므로 과거형 fostered를 현재분사 fostering으로 고쳐야 한다. ⓒ also awarded → was also awarded Earle가 TED Prize를 수여받는 수동의 의미이므로 능동태 awarded를 수동태 was awarded로 고쳐야 한다. ⓓ aim → aims 선행사 'a non-profit organization'이 단수이므로 복수 동사 aim을 단수 동사 aims로 고쳐야 한다. ⓔ to protect: 'Mission Blue's goal is to protect~'에서 to부정사가 주격 보어로 올바르게 쓰였다.

body:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 우리말과 일치하도록 <조건>에 맞게 영 작하시오.
Climate change is causing significant harm to the ocean, increasing its temperature and acidity. However, recent scientific insights position the ocean not merely as a victim, but as a potential remedy to this global crisis. 지구의 70%를 차지하는 바다는 대기 중 이산화탄소를 포집하는데 중요한 역할을 한 다. For thousands of years, marine ecosystems like kelp forests and marshes have been found to exceed plants on land in trapping and storing carbon. According to Dr. Carlos Duarte, a marine expert, the ocean holds 16 times more carbon than the land. This captured carbon is commonly known as "blue carbon," absorbed from the atmosphere and stored in the ocean. Blue carbon is mainly carbon dioxide that has dissolved directly in the ocean. While "black carbon" is a harmful material produced by burning fossil fuels and a significant contributor to climate change, blue carbon is stored in the ocean, preventing global warming.
조건 1. 접속사를 생략한 분사구문으로 문장을 시작할것
2. ocean, essential, cover, 70%, capture, carbon dioxide, atmosphere를 사용할 것
3. 필요시 단어를 추가하거나 형태를 변형할 것
4. 총 17단어로 쓸 것
→
answer: Covering 70% of Earth, the ocean plays an essential role in capturing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere.
solution: 지구의 70%를 차지하는'은 접속사를 생략한 분사구문으로 나타내야 하므로, cover를 현재분사 Covering으로 변형하여 문장 앞에 위치시킨다. '중요한 역할을 하다'는 play an essential role in으로 표현하며, in 뒤에는 동명사가 이어지므로 capture를 capturing으로 쓴다.

body:
다음 글을 읽고, 밑줄 친 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
Sylvia Earle's love for the ocean fueled her desire to explore further. In 1969, the same year astronauts first stepped on the moon, the Tektite Project allowed scientists to live in underwater habitats situated in the Virgin Islands. However, Earle was unable to participate in the project. "The people in charge just couldn't cope with the idea of men and women living together underwater," she said. 이듬해, 그녀는 전부 여성으로 구성된 텍타이트II 프로젝트의 리더로 선정되어 다른 해양학 자 네 명과 함께 해저 15미터에서 2주 동안 생활했다. She pushed the boundaries of underwater exploration and challenged gender stereotypes. Earle's residence on the reef allowed her to observe and understand the complexities of the ecosystem.
Her scientific findings were published, including the biology of coral reef fishes. The all female Tektite II crew became heroes upon their return to Earth's surface, receiving attention similar to that of the astronauts' historic moon landing.
조건 1. 접속사를 생략한 분사구문으로 문장을 시작할것
2. have, choose, lead, spend, live를 활용할것
3. 필요시 단어를 추가하거나 형태를 변형할 것
4. 앞의 빈칸에 5단어로, 뒤의 빈칸에 4단어로 각 각 쓸 것 (숫자를 영어로 표기할 것)
→The following year, _____ the all female Tektite II Project, she _____ 15 meters beneath the ocean's surface, along with four other oceanographers.
answer: having been chosen to lead, spent two weeks living
solution: 리더로 '선정된' 것이 주절보다 먼저 일어난 일이고, 주어 she가 선정되어지는 수동의 의미이므로 완료수동분사구문 'Having been chosen'으로 문장을 시작한다. '~하는 데 시간을 보내다'라는 의미의 'spend + 시간 + v-ing' 구문을 활용하여 spend를 'spent'로, live를 'living'으로 변형한다.

The Guardian of the Blue Heart of the Planet When most people were fascinated by the mysteries of exploring space, one remarkable individual appreciated the appeal of the ocean before many others, and eagerly explored the deep ocean. When people asked her, "Isn't it scary down there?" she would reply, "What's there to be afraid of? When I go down there, I delight in the life that I see." Long before others, this person recognized that not only is the ocean full of life, but that it also needs to be
ⓐexploited. She is the legendary marine biologist named Sylvia Earle. Sylvia Earle was born in 1935 in New Jersey. Having moved to Florida at the age of twelve, she began exploring the beaches and observing the ⓑdiverse marine life of the Gulf of Mexico. On her first birthday in Florida, her parents gifted her a pair of swimming goggles, perfect for someone who loved the ocean. Her father encouraged her, saying, "These will help you with your underwater explorations. Now all you have to do is dive in." With her goggles, Earle gained a ⓒclearer view of the ocean's wonders. At 17, she took her first deep dive, descending 10 meters in a lake wearing the diving suit that belonged to her friend's father. Earle was ⓓthrilled to observe fish while breathing naturally underwater. As Earle experienced the excitement of diving, her desire to explore grew, and she eventually became one of the first marine scientists to use scuba equipment. Her innate sense of adventure and curiosity ⓔhindered her academic journey, ultimately leading her to become a pioneer in ocean exploration and conservation.

body:
다음 글의 분위기로 가장 적절한 것은?
Sai woke to Vivaldi's violin concerto in C minor, Il Sospetto (The Suspicion). He lay still for a minute, letting the music wash over him like a breeze. Tilly had woken him right at the end of a light sleep cycle, the best time. He felt great: cheerful, optimistic, ready to jump out of bed, which is what he did next. "Tilly, that's an inspired choice for a wake-up song." "Of course," Tilly spoke from the camera speaker on the nightstand. "Who knows your tastes and moods better than I?" The voice, though electronic, was affectionate and playful. Sai went into the shower. "Remember to wear the new shoes today," Tilly now spoke to him from the camera speaker in the ceiling. "Why?" "You have a date after work." "Oh, the new girl. I know you told me—" "I'll tell you all about her after work. I'm sure you will have fallen in love with her even before the dinner ends. The compatibility score is very high." Sai looked forward to the date. But first he still had to get through his day's work as a legal assistant. "What do you recommend for breakfast this morning?" "You are scheduled to attend the lunch meeting for the Davis case at eleven. I suggest you go light on the breakfast, maybe just a banana." "Do I have time to make my own coffee?" "You do. Traffic is light this morning. But I suggest you go to this new juice bar along the way instead. I can get you a coupon code." "But I really want coffee." "Trust me, you'll love the juice." Sai smiled. "Okay, Tilly. You always know best."
choices: tense and mysterious
cheerful and upbeat
gloomy and melancholic
urgent and stressful
lonely and sorrowful
solution: ② Sai는 Vivaldi 음악에 맞춰 기분 좋게 기상하고, Tilly와 유쾌한 대화를 나누며 데이트를 기대하고, Tilly의 주스 바 제안에도 흔쾌히 동의하며 미소 짓는다. 글 전반에 걸쳐 경쾌하고 활기찬 분위기가 일관되게 유지되므로 cheerful(유쾌한) and upbeat(활기찬)가 정답이다. ① tense: 긴장된, mysterious: 신비로운 ③ gloomy: 우울한, melancholic: 침울한 ④ urgent: 긴박한, stressful: 스트레스받는 ⑤ lonely: 외로운, sorrowful: 슬픈

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Stepping out of his apartment, Sai saw Jenny, a weird neighbor who always covered her face with ski goggles and her hair with a long dark scarf. She complained again about ⓐthe camera installed over his door. Although Sai and Jenny both belonged to the digital native generation, he could tell she was the kind of girl
ⓑwho refused to use Centillion email or get a ShareAll account, like Sai's grandmother's friends. "Jenny, I have a right to install anything I want over my door. And I want Tilly to keep an eye on my door when I'm away." "But your camera will record visitors to my place, too, because we share this hallway." "So?" "I don't want Tilly to know any of my social relationships." Sai rolled his eyes. "What do you have to hide?" "That's not the point—" "Yeah, yeah, civil liberties, privacy, blah blah blah ..." Sai was sick of arguing with people like Jenny. He had made the same point countless times: Centillion is not some big scary government. It's a private company,
ⓒwhose motto happens to be "Make things better!" Just because you want to live in the dark ages ⓓdoesn't mean the rest of us shouldn't enjoy the benefits of ubiquitous computing. "Tilly doesn't just tell you what you want," Jenny shouted. "She tells you what to think. Do you even know what you really want any more?" Sai paused for a moment. "Do you?" she pressed. What a ridiculous question. He kept on walking. "Freak," he said quietly, expecting Tilly to agree with him from his phone earpiece and ⓔmake some joke to cheer up him. But (A)Tilly said nothing.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (A)"Tilly said nothing"이 의미하는 바 로 가장 적절한 것은?
choices: Tilly was suddenly disconnected due to a temporary network error
Tilly was showing respect for Jenny's opinion by remaining silent
Jenny's point that Tilly controls Sai's thoughts might actually be valid
Tilly was preparing to report Jenny to Centillion for making false claims
Tilly wanted Sai to solve his conflict with his neighbor on his own
solution: ③ 밑줄 친 부분 앞에서 Sai는 Jenny를 "별종(Freak)"이라 부르며 Tilly가 자신의 편을 들어 농담으로 기분을 풀어주기를 기대했다. 그러나 평소 Sai의 모든 일상을 관리하며 적극적으로 반응해 온 Tilly가 아무 말도 하지 않은 것은, Jenny의 "Do you even know what you really want anymore?"라는 질문이 단순한 억측이 아닐 수 있음을 암시한다. 따라서 밑줄 친 부분은 Jenny의 말이 어느 정도 타당했을 수 있다는 의미이다.

보기 the / sure / end / you / I'm / with / will / dinner / even / fall / love / before / in / her
조건 1. <보기>의 단어들을 배열하여 영작하되, 시제와 어법에 맞게 단어를 변형할 것
2. 단어 변형 시 필요한 단어를 1개 추가할 것
3. 미래완료 시제로 쓸 것
→
answer: I'm sure you will have fallen in love with her even before the dinner ends.
solution: '~라고 확신하다'라는 의미의 'I'm sure' 구문 뒤에 미래완료 시제(will have p.p.)를 적용하여 'fall'을 'have fallen'으로 형태 변형하고, 시간 부사절(before절)에서는 현재시제가 미래를 대용하므로 3인칭 단수 주어 'the dinner'에 맞춰 'end'를 'ends'로 형태 변형하여 문법적으로 올바르게 쓴다.

Stepping out of his apartment, Sai saw Jenny, a weird neighbor who always covered her face with ski goggles and her hair with a long dark scarf. She complained again about the camera installed over his door. Although Sai and Jenny both belonged to the digital native generation, he could tell she was the kind of girl who refused to use Centillion email or get a ShareAll account, like Sai's grandmother's friends. "Jenny, I have a right to install anything I want over my door. And I want Tilly to keep an eye on my door when I'm away." "But your camera will record visitors to my place, too, because we share this hallway." "So?" "I don't want Tilly to know any of my social relationships." Sai rolled his eyes. "What do you have to hide?" "That's not the point—" "Yeah, yeah, civil liberties, privacy, blah blah blah ..." Sai was sick of arguing with people like Jenny. He had made the same point countless times:
Centillion is not some big scary government. It's a private company, whose motto happens to be "Make things better!" 위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution: ③ⓒ were now made just accept → were now made to just accept 사역동사 make의 수동태(be made) 뒤에는 원형부정사가 아닌 to부정사가 와야 하므로, accept를 to accept로 고쳐야 한다. ① 선행사인 'Her apartment'를 부연 설명하며 목적어가 빠진 절을 이끌고 있으므로, 계속적 용법의 관계대명사 which가 올바르게 쓰였다. ② '~하는 것을 중단하다'라는 의미로 동명사 questioning을 목적어로 취하고 있으므로, stop이 올바르게 쓰였다. ④ 주절의 주어인 he가 공포를 느끼는 수동의 주체이므로, 과거분사 Horrified가 분사구문으로 올바르게 쓰였다. ⑤ 뒤에 명사구인 'all their precautions'가 왔으므로, 명사를 목적어로 취하는 전치사 despite가 올바르게 쓰였다.

Sai and Jenny looked at each other. "What?" "We want people who can see through Tilly's suggestions, detecting her imperfections. Because you can see her flaws, you'll be the best at figuring out what Tilly's still missing and where she's gone too far. It's the perfect match." "What if we refuse to join you but tell the world what you've done?" "No one would believe you. We'll make sure that nothing you write can be found. On the Net, if it can't be found by Centillion, it doesn't exist." Sai knew that he was right. Rinn continued:
"Without Tilly, you can't do your jobs or even remember things. We are now a race of cyborgs. The data you tried to destroy are electronic extensions of yourself. That night Sai asked Tilly to set the wake-up song to Sinatra's My Way and to turn herself off. The camera buzzed, followed Sai to bed, and shut off.
But a red light continued to blink, slowly, in the darkness.
보기 succeed / even / destroying / Tilly / if / you / eventually / it / replaced / within / by / in / worse / weeks / will / have / something / been

body:
다음 글을 읽고 물음에 답하시오.
Many people fear that artificial intelligence will pose a danger if it develops consciousness. Could a piece of AI software "wake up," ⓐprioritize its desires above ours, and endanger humanity's existence? Some thinkers imagine extreme, ⓑ dystopian possibilities. For example, think of an AI that was originally built with the goal of decreasing suffering in the world. Would it not decide at some point to eliminate humanity for the good of the rest of life on Earth? Others are more optimistic. They say that a conscious AI may be less dangerous than a non-conscious one. In humans, the mental process that puts the brakes on
ⓒmoral behavior is empathy, the ability to feel what other people feel. Conscious, superintelligent AIs could eventually develop this ability and care about us more than non-conscious ones would. Some people insist that this concern about AI's consciousness is
ⓓmisplaced . They believe AI is dangerous not because it is conscious, but because (A) . So, whether AI develops consciousness or not, the most important thing to do is to program "human" ethics into it. 1회차 실전 모의고사 What do you think? Once a superintelligent AI— conscious or not—is built, it can improve itself and start changing the world, and it might be difficult to control.
Then, is it possible to create superintelligent AI with goals, values, and ethical codes that make it ⓔfavorable and even helpful to humans?

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ의 문맥상 의미로 어색한 것은?
solution: ③ moral → immoral 공감(empathy)은 비도덕적 행동을 억제하는 심리적 작용이므로, moral(도덕적인)은 immoral(비도덕적인)로 바꿔야 문맥에 맞다. ⓐ prioritize: 우선시하다 ⓑ dystopian: 디스토피아적인, 암울한 ⓓ misplaced: 잘못 짚은 ⓔ favorable: 호의적인

Many people fear that artificial intelligence will pose a danger if it develops consciousness. Could a piece of AI software "wake up," prioritize its desires above ours, and endanger humanity's existence? Some thinkers imagine extreme, dystopian possibilities. For example, think of an AI that was originally built with the goal of decreasing suffering in the world. Would it not decide at some point to eliminate humanity for the good of the rest of life on Earth? Others are more optimistic. They say that a conscious AI may be less dangerous than a non- conscious one. In humans, the mental process that puts the brakes on immoral behavior is empathy, the ability to feel what other people feel. Conscious, superintelligent AIs could eventually develop this ability and care about us more than non-conscious ones would. 2회차 실전 모의고사 Some people insist that this concern about AI's consciousness is misplaced. They believe AI is dangerous not because it is conscious, but because it is built without complex ethics. So, whether AI develops consciousness or not, the most important thing to do is to program "human" ethics into it.
What do you think? Once a superintelligent AI— conscious or not—is built, it can improve itself and start changing the world, and it might be difficult to control. Then, is it possible to create superintelligent AI with goals, values, and ethical codes that make it favorable and even helpful to humans? While views on conscious AI range from (A) _____ to (B) _____ , many agree that whether or not AI develops (C) _____ , embedding human (D) _____ into it is the key to ensuring it benefits humanity.
(A) _____ (B)
(C) _____ (D) _____
solution: (A) 지문에서 일부 사상가들은 AI 의식에 대해 극단적이고 암울한 가능성을 상상한다고 했으므로 dystopian이 적절하다. (B) 반면 다른 이들은 의식 있는 AI가 덜 위험할 수 있다는 낙관적 견해를 보이고 있으므로 optimistic이 적절하다. (C) 지문에서 "whether AI develops consciousness or not"이라고 했으므로 consciousness가 적절하다. (D) 지문에서 의식 여부와 관계없이 AI에 인간적 윤리를 프로그래밍하는 것이 가장 중요하다고 했으므로 ethics가 적절하다.

solution: ㉡ 'be entitled to-v'는 '~할 권리가 있다, 자격이 주어지다'라는 의미의 수동태 관용 표현이다. 주어인 Sai가 법적으로 그러한 권리를 '부여받은(수동)' 상태이므로 과거분사 형태인 entitled가 되어야 한다. ㉤ 이 문장은 'What + a/an + 형용사 + 명사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순의 감탄문이다. 주어가 단수 대명사인 it이므로 과거 시제 동사 역시 단수형인 was로 일치시켜야 한다. 가정법 문장이 아니므로 were를 쓸 수 없다. ㉦ 대명사가 가리키는 대상은 문맥상 단수 명사인 a document 또는 a specific legal template 중 하나를 지칭하는 것이므로, 복수 대명사 them이 아니라 단수 대명사 it으로 받아야 올바르다 ㉠ 명사 the surveillance camera를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사로 적절하다. ㉢ 5형식 동사 require는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취하므로 monitor는 적절하다. ㉣ 선행사인 a private corporation과 뒤의 명사 explicit motto가 소유의 관계(~의 명확한 모토)를 이루므로, 소유격 관계대명사 whose가 올바르게 쓰였다. ㉥ 5형식 동사 expect는 목적격 보어로 to부정사를 취한다. (expect + 목적어 + to-v) 따라서 to chime in은 어법상 올바르다. 따라서 어법상 틀린 것의 개수는 3개로, 정답은 ③이다.

→
solution: 본문에서 'the ability to feel what other people feel'과 동격으로 쓰인 단어는 empathy(공감)이며, 문제의 문장은 '다른 사람들이 느끼는 것을 느끼는 능력을 라고 부른다'라는 의미이므로 빈칸에는 empathy가 적절하다.

Such gaps in data sharing may inevitably cause your user profile to become incomplete —" "Yes, stop at once." Accompanied by a sharp electronic beep, Tilly deactivated herself. Ellen gazed at him, her eyes wide and her mouth agape in sheer astonishment. Sai offered a gentle smile. "It feels refreshing occasionally to just exist as ourselves without Tilly's intervention, wouldn't you agree?" Ellen appeared thoroughly perplexed.
